title: Standard DESeq2 differential expression and effect-size reporting

sources.locator: Pasilla context and differential expression/shrinkage, lines 642-719

scientific_use: Fit the negative-binomial model to a gene-by-sample raw count matrix and sample metadata, test a treatment contrast, extract log2 fold changes and p-values, and shrink effect estimates for stable visualization/ranking.
tool_role_basis: The vignette constructs a DESeqDataSet and applies DESeq, results, and lfcShrink; the package DESCRIPTION describes inference using a negative-binomial model. The task would use existing package operations.
inputs: Unnormalized integer gene-level count matrix with genes as rows and samples as columns; sample metadata rows must be reordered to exactly match count columns.
Factor-valued condition and design formula such as ~ condition; Pasilla fixture includes condition and sequencing type.
outputs: DESeqDataSet carrying fitted model and intermediate estimates.
Per-gene results including base mean, log2 fold change, standard error, statistic, p-value, and adjusted p-value; optionally shrunken LFC for visualization/ranking.
dependencies: R and DESeq2 plus Bioconductor dependencies listed in DESCRIPTION.
apeglm is an optional package for the illustrated type=apeglm shrinkage.
Input count table and aligned sample annotation; no alignment/counting stage is performed in this workflow.
evidence: DESCRIPTION package description and dependency fields
limitations: No execution was performed.
The packaged count matrix contents were not downloaded or previewed; exact dimensions and gene identifiers remain unchecked.
The vignette links the original Pasilla data package and cites Brooks et al.; package-level source processing details need separate inspection.
Task author must define contrast, filtering, shrinkage method availability, and deterministic grading outputs.

title: Import transcript quantifications into a gene-level DESeq2 object

sources.locator: Transcript abundance files and tximport/tximeta, lines 256-359

scientific_use: Import transcript abundance estimates from Salmon and summarize/link transcripts to genes, then construct a gene-level DESeqDataSet while retaining the tximport-derived information used by downstream DESeq2 analysis.
tool_role_basis: The documented workflow composes Salmon output, tximport, and DESeq2 constructors; it does not implement those algorithms.
inputs: Salmon quant.sf files (the vignette demonstration uses quant.sf.gz paths from tximportData).
Sample table including run identifiers and condition; demonstration assigns artificial A/B labels.
Transcript-to-gene mapping table tx2gene.
outputs: tximport object and DESeqDataSet created by DESeqDataSetFromTximport, ready for the standard DE workflow.
dependencies: Salmon quantification produced upstream; tximport and DESeq2 packages; tximportData is used only to locate demonstration inputs; readr reads the mapping table.
limitations: The vignette says demonstration condition labels are artificial; biological design and suitability of these example quantifications were not checked.
tximportData archive contents, access terms, and exact upstream study identity were not inspected.
The task author must supply compatible quantification files and a correct tx2gene table; no Salmon run is part of the documented DESeq2 stage.

title: Control for sequencing type and extract factor contrasts
scientific_use: Re-fit the Pasilla data with sequencing type as a covariate and condition as the effect of interest, then extract both the treatment effect and a sequencing-type contrast.
tool_role_basis: The example changes the design formula and calls DESeq/results on a DESeqDataSet; it composes package API operations.
inputs: Pasilla counts and aligned sample metadata with condition and sequencing type fields.
Existing DESeqDataSet or equivalent reconstructed from the bundled raw counts; design ~ type + condition.
outputs: Fitted multifactor model and result tables for treatment and type contrasts.
dependencies: DESeq2 and the same raw counts/metadata used by the standard workflow.
Factor reference levels and names must be controlled because default results refer to the final design term.
evidence: vignettes/DESeq2.Rmd lines 1116-1187; the design is set to ~ type + condition and results contrast type single versus paired
limitations: Pasilla sample type is sequencing protocol metadata, not a biological treatment; confirm the intended interpretation and estimability before task use.
No execution or design-rank check was performed.

title: Interaction and likelihood-ratio tests for grouped and time-series effects

sources.locator: Interactions, time-series experiments, and LRT, lines 1509-1681

scientific_use: Estimate genotype-specific condition effects and test whether effects differ across genotypes using an interaction model; use full-versus-reduced negative-binomial GLM likelihood ratio tests to test multiple terms, including time or interaction terms.
tool_role_basis: The source demonstrates DESeq2 design formulas, contrasts and test='LRT'; simulated plotting data in the interaction illustration are explanatory fixtures, not a new analysis algorithm.
inputs: Raw count matrix and sample metadata with relevant genotype, condition, or time factors; full design formula.
For LRT, a scientifically chosen reduced design nested within the full design.
For interaction effect extraction, explicit coefficient names/reference levels or combined-group contrasts.
outputs: LRT result table testing the extra terms in the full model; coefficient/contrast results for genotype-specific effects.
dependencies: DESeq2; valid, estimable full/reduced models and enough replication for intended inference.
evidence: vignettes/DESeq2.Rmd lines 1509-1622 describe grouped-factor shortcut and interaction coefficients; lines 1624-1638 describe time-series contrasts; lines 1640-1681 define and call LRT
limitations: No concrete biological time-series dataset is identified in this section; the RNA-seq workflow link is a follow-up lead.
The interaction plots use simulated counts, so they support explanation rather than an observed-data task.
Task design must select a specific null hypothesis and ensure full/reduced formula nesting.

title: Transform counts for sample-level quality assessment and visualization

sources.locator: Count data transformations and sample QC plots, lines 1191-1440

scientific_use: Apply normalized variance-stabilizing or regularized-log transformations for clustering and visualization, inspect sample distances and PCA by experimental covariates, and use the transformed matrix for QA rather than differential testing.
tool_role_basis: The vignette calls DESeq2 transformation and plotting APIs (vst, rlog, plotPCA) and plotting packages; it does not implement the transformation algorithms.
inputs: DESeqDataSet with raw counts and sample metadata; fitted dispersions/design where available.
Optional blind setting chosen according to QA versus downstream analysis purpose.
outputs: DESeqTransform normalized log-scale assay, sample distance matrix/heatmap, and PCA coordinates/plot.
dependencies: DESeq2; pheatmap and RColorBrewer for illustrated heatmaps; ggplot2 for customized PCA; vsn for meanSdPlot comparison.
evidence: vignettes/DESeq2.Rmd lines 1193-1289 explain VST/rlog and blind dispersion; lines 1356-1440 show heatmaps, sample distances, and PCA on the Pasilla DESeqTransform
limitations: This is a diagnostic/visualization workflow, not a differential-expression test or a basis for claiming all genes have equal variance.
The vignette reports relative runtime behavior but this pass did not measure runtime.
No generated plots were executed or visually assessed.

title: Diagnose and handle count outliers with Cook's distance
scientific_use: Inspect gene/sample Cook's distances and understand the default result flagging or count replacement behavior; optionally disable automation for manual review when many outliers are present.
tool_role_basis: The documented workflow uses DESeq and results built-in diagnostics and accesses stored assays; no scientific method implementation is modified.
inputs: Fitted DESeqDataSet retaining Cook's distances and, if applicable, replacement counts.
Sample count/design metadata, particularly replicate count and model degrees of freedom.
outputs: Cook's distance matrix, result p-values set to NA for flagged genes, optional replacement-count assay, and diagnostic plots for review.
dependencies: DESeq2 standard model fit and results; manual biological/sample-quality interpretation for investigation of many outliers.
evidence: vignettes/DESeq2.Rmd lines 1908-1951 describe Cook's distance, flagging, and replacement; lines 1953-1970 recommend PCA/boxplot review for extensive outliers
limitations: Automatic thresholds depend on sample size and model parameter count; task author must retain these settings and avoid treating the diagnostic as proof of technical error.
No data were executed or outliers inspected in this pass.

title: Test whether gene effects exceed a specified log2 fold-change threshold

sources.locator: Tests of log2 fold change above or below a threshold, lines 2070-2104

scientific_use: Use results() Wald tests with lfcThreshold and altHypothesis to test directional or absolute effect-size claims, and compare the four null/alternative formulations using result tables and MA plots.
tool_role_basis: The documented workflow calls the existing results API with each of its four alternative hypotheses; it does not implement a statistical test.
inputs: DESeqDataSet after DESeq model fit and a named coefficient.
Nonnegative log2 fold-change threshold and one of greaterAbs, lessAbs, greater, or less.
outputs: Per-gene threshold-test statistics, p-values and adjusted p-values; optional MA plots showing threshold bounds.
dependencies: DESeq2 standard model workflow; coefficient name and threshold must match the scientific question.
evidence: vignettes/DESeq2.Rmd lines 2070-2104 defines the four alternatives and demonstrates threshold 0.5 on the Pasilla dds
limitations: The vignette illustration uses the same Pasilla object built earlier; no execution was done.
Task author must explicitly define the effect-size direction and threshold and must not confuse null and alternative hypotheses.

title: Extract linear contrasts among factor levels and model coefficients
scientific_use: Construct a results table for a chosen comparison among factor levels or a linear combination of fitted log2 fold-change coefficients, including contrasts that combine or subtract coefficients.
tool_role_basis: The vignette demonstrates results(dds, contrast=...) and points to coefficient names/numeric contrast vectors; all inference uses the existing DESeq2 API.
inputs: Fitted DESeqDataSet with factor-level design or named model coefficients.
Contrast as factor/numerator/denominator, a list of coefficient names to add/subtract, or numeric coefficient vector.
outputs: Per-feature log2 fold change and Wald test result table for the specified linear contrast.
dependencies: DESeq2 fitted model; correct reference levels and resultsNames(dds); contrast must encode the intended biological comparison.
evidence: vignettes/DESeq2.Rmd lines 1476-1505 define contrasts as linear combinations and show factor and coefficient forms
limitations: The example is API guidance and has no dataset tied to this subsection.
No contrast was executed; author must verify model coefficient interpretation and estimability.

title: Inspect the independent filtering threshold used for multiple testing
scientific_use: Inspect how results() uses mean normalized counts as a filter statistic and selects a quantile threshold to increase discoveries at significance level alpha; compare default adjusted p-values with independentFiltering=FALSE.
tool_role_basis: The vignette uses the DESeq2 results API and its metadata outputs to inspect built-in independent filtering; it does not implement the filter.
inputs: Fitted DESeqDataSet and results table, significance level alpha, and optionally filtering disabled for comparison.
outputs: Adjusted p-values with non-passing genes set to NA under default filtering; metadata including selected threshold, filter rejection counts, and alpha for diagnostic visualization.
dependencies: DESeq2 results(); default implementation calls genefilter filtered_p per vignette.
evidence: vignettes/DESeq2.Rmd lines 2021-2066 describes mean-normalized-count filtering and metadata diagnostics
limitations: The section uses previously created Pasilla results but does not independently detail the dataset.
Filtering can complicate benchmark comparisons because NA adjusted p-values need an explicit scoring policy; the policy is task-specific.
No filter thresholds or counts were computed in this pass.

title: Single-cell DESeq2 settings and pseudobulk boundary
scientific_use: Apply the vignette's specified settings for individual-cell count matrices (LRT, useT, low minmu, disable count replacement, consider scran size factors and glmGamPoi) and distinguish this setting from pseudobulk comparisons within cell type.
tool_role_basis: This is documented configuration of existing DESeq2 and adjacent packages, not tool development.
inputs: Single-cell gene-by-cell count matrix and cell metadata; cell-type heterogeneity and design are material context.
For pseudobulk alternative, aggregate counts by biological sample within cell type before differential analysis (aggregation procedure is not specified here).
outputs: Fitted single-cell differential-expression model/results under recommended settings, or pseudobulk results from a separate upstream aggregation stage.
dependencies: DESeq2; optional scran for sum-factor size factors and glmGamPoi for faster fitting; zinbwave integration is linked as a separate option.
evidence: vignettes/DESeq2.Rmd lines 1837-1890; explicit caveat states recommendations target individual cells in heterogeneous mixtures while pseudobulk obviates these changes
limitations: No single-cell dataset or runnable end-to-end example is supplied in this section.
Recommendations are scoped to individual cells in heterogeneous mixtures; task design must not apply them blindly to pseudobulk.
Linked glmGamPoi, zinbwave and simulation repository were not inspected; no validation was performed.
